concepts.title: LAUNCH WINDOW

comic: Earth and Mars go around the Sun at different speeds, so the distance between them keeps changing.
The most energy-efficient trip opens only about once every 26 months: the LAUNCH WINDOW.
Your plan: launch {LAUNCH}, {DV} km/s of Δv. In this game, Spirit's real dates need about 5.7 km/s.
Spirit launched on June 10, 2003 and Opportunity on July 7, 2003. Both landed in January 2004.
podcast: Why did both rovers leave Earth in the summer of 2003?
Because of the launch window. Earth and Mars line up for the most energy-efficient trip only about once every 26 months.
And what happens if you launch outside it?
The same trip needs much more Δv, which means more fuel. Your plan used {DV} km/s.
So the date is a mission decision, not just a calendar choice.
Exactly. Spirit launched on June 10, 2003 and Opportunity on July 7, 2003.
flash: How often do Earth and Mars line up for the most energy-efficient trip?
About every 26 months. MER's two rockets launched in the 2003 window.
practice: Why did Spirit and Opportunity launch in mid-2003?
Earth and Mars lined up for an efficient trip: the launch window
Mars was at its closest point to the Sun
The rockets could only fly in summer

concepts.why: Earth and Mars line up for the most energy-efficient trip only about once every 26 months. Launching inside that window needs less Δv, so less fuel. That is why MER's two rockets launched in the 2003 window.

concepts.title: WATER CLUES

reason.ok: You collected {SAMPLES} sample(s); {STRONG} had a strong water clue.

comic: Some minerals form only when water is present. They are clues to the wet past of Mars.
Opportunity found tiny hematite spheres, nicknamed "blueberries". Hematite typically forms in water.
In your hunt: {SAMPLES} sample(s), {STRONG} with a strong water clue.
Gypsum veins form when water moves through cracks. Jarosite forms in acidic water.
podcast: How can a rock tell us there was water?
Some minerals only form in water. Hematite "blueberries" are one of them, and Opportunity found many.
What else counts as a strong clue?
Gypsum veins form when water moves through cracks, and jarosite forms in acidic water.
In this mission you brought home {STRONG} strong clue(s).
And remember: weak evidence does not mean there was NO water. It means we need more evidence.
flash: Which mineral, nicknamed "blueberries", did Opportunity find?
Hematite spheres. Hematite typically forms in water.
practice: Which mineral did Opportunity find that typically forms in water?
Hematite "blueberries"
Ordinary basalt
Windblown dust
Hematite typically forms in water. Opportunity found it at Meridiani Planum.
concepts.why: Rovers cannot see old lakes, but minerals remember them. Hematite, gypsum and jarosite form in water, so finding them is evidence that liquid water once existed. Basalt and windblown dust are not water clues on their own.
check: Which mineral is a clue that water was once present?

concepts.title: INSTRUMENTS

reason.ok: Your rover carried {ATHENA} of the 6 Athena instruments{MISSING}.

comic: Each instrument answers a different question about a rock.
Mini-TES spots water minerals from far away. APXS measures a rock's chemistry. Mössbauer identifies iron minerals like hematite.
Your rover carried {ATHENA} of the 6 Athena instruments{MISSING}.
The real rovers carried the Athena payload: Pancam, Mini-TES, Microscopic Imager, APXS, Mössbauer and the Rock Abrasion Tool.
podcast: Why not just take the newest instruments?
Each tool answers one question. APXS measures chemistry, Mössbauer finds iron minerals like hematite.
And PIXL? It is great for chemistry.
PIXL was built for a newer rover, Perseverance. Spirit and Opportunity used the Athena payload.
Your rover carried {ATHENA} of the 6 Athena instruments.
Without the right instrument, a rock's clue stays unreadable. That is what happened in Rock Hunter.
flash: Which Athena instrument measured the chemistry of a rock?
APXS. (Mössbauer identified iron minerals like hematite.)
practice: Which instrument was built for the newer Perseverance rover, not for Spirit and Opportunity?
PIXL
APXS
Pancam
PIXL was built for Perseverance. Spirit and Opportunity used APXS for chemistry.
concepts.why: Spirit and Opportunity carried the Athena payload: Pancam, Mini-TES, Microscopic Imager, APXS, Mössbauer and the Rock Abrasion Tool. Each answers a different question, so the kit decides which clues a rover can read.
check: Which instrument did Spirit and Opportunity use to measure a rock's chemistry?

concepts.title: DATA TO EARTH

reason.ok: {PACKETS} of 3 packets reached the orbiter; your comms plan was "{QUALITY}".

comic: Spirit and Opportunity sent most of their data through orbiters: Mars Odyssey and Mars Global Surveyor.
Rover → orbiter → Deep Space Network on Earth. An orbiter pass lasts only 2 to 8 minutes.
Your mission: {PACKETS} of 3 packets reached the orbiter. Your plan was "{QUALITY}".
A packet that does not get out is not lost: it stays in the rover's flash memory for a later pass.
podcast: Spirit and Opportunity sent most of their data through orbiters: Mars Odyssey and Mars Global Surveyor.
What happens if a packet does not reach the orbiter?
It is not lost: it stays in the rover's flash memory, which keeps data even when the power is off.
So it can be sent later?
Yes, on another pass. The limit is not time, it is space: each rover had 256 MB of flash memory.
In your mission, {PACKETS} of 3 packets reached the orbiter.
flash: What happens to data that does not reach the orbiter?
It stays in the rover's flash memory and can be sent on a later pass.
practice: How did most of Spirit and Opportunity's data reach Earth?
Relayed through orbiters like Mars Odyssey
Carried back by a return rocket
Sent by laser from the rover
By the end of the prime mission, 89% of the data came home through UHF relays.
concepts.why: An orbiter passes over the rover for only 2 to 8 minutes, so small, valuable results (like rover health and spectrometer data) should go first. By the end of the prime mission, 89% of the rovers' data had come home through UHF relays.
check: If a data packet does not reach the orbiter, what happens?
It stays saved in the rover's memory and is sent on another pass
You must wait 26 months for the next window

concepts.title: SPACECRAFT DESIGN

reason.ok: {MATCHES} of 4 spacecraft choices match the real MER design.

comic: The cruise stage carried the lander and the rover to Mars.
Power in space came from solar panels on the cruise stage.
MER talked to Earth with low-gain and medium-gain X-band antennas.
The spacecraft spun at about 2 rpm during cruise to stay stable. Your design: {MATCHES} of 4 choices match MER.
podcast: How did the spacecraft stay pointed on the way to Mars?
It was spin-stabilized: it spun at about 2 rpm during cruise.
And the antennas still worked while it spun?
Yes. Its wide-beam antennas could still reach Earth while it spun.
Low-gain and medium-gain X-band antennas, right?
Right. Your design matched {MATCHES} of 4 of the real choices.
flash: How did the MER spacecraft stay stable during cruise?
It was spin-stabilized: it spun at about 2 rpm.
practice: What powered the MER spacecraft during the trip to Mars?
Solar panels on the cruise stage
A nuclear battery
Batteries charged only on Earth
Solar panels on the cruise stage powered the trip.
concepts.why: A spinning cruise stage stays stable, and its wide-beam antennas can still reach Earth while it spins. Solar panels gave power, and low-gain plus medium-gain X-band antennas kept the link.
check: How did the MER spacecraft stay stable during cruise?
